bigPicture: The IDE is becoming the operating system for AI-augmented work — and the infrastructure underneath it is already buckling under the weight of what we're building on top.

dataPoints.context: Karpathy's 'bigger IDE' post is the most resonant signal of the day — the industry knows the tooling layer is the real battleground
Anthropic ships 1M context as default for Claude Code — agentic coding just got full-codebase awareness
Karpathy's 'intelligence brownouts' post — autoresearch labs wiped by a single OAuth outage exposes how fragile AI-heavy workflows actually are
Cursor's agentic coding benchmark becomes instant industry reference — whoever defines the eval defines the market

tldr: The IDE wars are heating up: Cursor ships benchmarks, plugins (Hugging Face, Datadog), and eval methodology while Karpathy argues the IDE must evolve into an agent orchestrator — not die
Anthropic goes all-in on agentic: 1M context GA, Opus 4.6 as Claude Code default, generative UI, and explicit signals that knowledge work is next after coding

Infrastructure fragility is the elephant in the room — Karpathy's autoresearch labs wiped by an OAuth outage proves AI-heavy workflows need the same resilience engineering as traditional production systems
Real enterprise AI is quietly shipping: Honeywell runs air-gapped RAG for field techs, Google puts Gemini in Maps, Perplexity rolls out agentic Computer to all iOS users

The agent tooling stack is maturing fast: context compression (Context Gateway), agent memory debates (filesystem vs graphs vs embeddings), visual multi-agent collaboration (Spine Swarm), and early 'SEO for agents' playbooks
